candidates.name: Existing UAR full_harness_v1 authority plus Bossfang consumer adapter
candidates.fit_for_gap: F1/F5: one executor, admission identity, observation and cancellation

evidence.claim: Pinned source reserves owner/workspace/admission identity and advertises process-ephemeral recovery; no replacement provider needed.
Shared admission, replay stream, approval ID, revision-checked cancel/detach already exist.
Existing initiative consumer groups remain pending; link rather than duplicate.

risks: No process restart recovery or steer; epoch/retention loss means unknown outcome.
Integration gate remains pending; exact request digest includes credential material.
Existing owner/file claims must be reconciled before writes.
candidates.decision_rationale: Wrap the existing provider with an explicit execution adapter outside the Bossfang model loop; adapt the consumer, not rebuild UAR execution.

candidates.name: jsonwebtoken 11.0.0 with existing UAR verifier
candidates.fit_for_gap: F2/F3: retained cryptography underneath corrected issuer/key/tenant policy

evidence.claim: Repository search resolves the existing upstream.
Validation supports configured issuer/audience/required claims; pinned source overrides ambiguous latest prose.
Latest stable 11.1.0, 11.0.0 unyanked; no upgrade proposed.
UAR explicitly supplies nbf flag and inserts required issuer/audience claims when configured.

risks: Library defaults do not establish remote application policy.
JWKS freshness and role attenuation are application responsibilities.
No vulnerability audit or compile compatibility check performed.
candidates.decision_rationale: Retain pinned primitives; build the small policy corrections above them. Adopt means reuse installed dependency, not change its version.

candidates.name: rmcp 3.1.2 and current UAR owner/run-scoped MCP integration
candidates.fit_for_gap: F4/F6: transport reuse, principal-session boundary and resource grants

evidence.claim: Official Rust SDK found by repository search.
Latest SessionManager API uses session identifiers; this is documentation context, not proof of pinned principal enforcement.
Registry reports 3.5.1 latest; no upgrade or security fix inferred.
UAR router uses LocalSessionManager and legacy_session_mode=true; pinned SDK paths inspected in review.

risks: Pinned docs failed through web fetch; local 3.1.2 source remains authority.
Cross-principal session consequence is untested.
Changing SDK versions alone does not establish application ownership.
candidates.decision_rationale: Retain rmcp 3.1.2 and current transport unchanged. Any new owner/session binding requires recorded production-router reproduction under F6-REPRODUCTION; this candidate is not authorization to implement that remediation.

candidates.name: oauth2-rs 5.0.0 resource client
candidates.fit_for_gap: F4/G7-A: potential host-side resource token acquisition/refresh

evidence.claim: General Rust OAuth client fits more broadly than provider-specific/HTTP-framework search alternatives.
PKCE, client credentials, refresh, introspection/revocation and custom HTTP client support; not a complete MCP authorization service.
Latest stable 5.0.0; age alone does not establish abandonment or security.
HTTP client dependency compatibility must be checked against existing UAR reqwest boundaries.

risks: Production receiver/IdP unspecified; no unconditional adoption.
Native RFC8693 exchange support not established by fetched examples.
Does not supply tenant policy, token storage or MCP discovery contract.
No install/build/advisory audit performed.
If selected for a Rust host, use existing application reqwest 0.12; never pass reqwest_mcp 0.13.4 as that client. Hosting module remains blocked on receiver inventory.
candidates.decision_rationale: Promote to adopt/adapt only when a named receiver requires a supported flow and existing host clients cannot satisfy it; no new daemon.

candidates.name: The Boss exact prepared-invocation admission and UAR approval authority
candidates.fit_for_gap: F7/G7-B: payload-bound approval, one claim per effect and safe projection

evidence.claim: Claim-before-effect and unknown-outcome handling are implemented.
Prior research ran this production bridge with fixture effects; no new run or product certification.
Full-harness approval forwarding requires approval ID and expected task revision.

risks: Legacy root response still requires migration.
The bridge fixture does not certify all clients.
Tool-result canaries require separate exposure policy.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reuse exact admission, migrate client/root compatibility; do not replace it with a generic login or run-level approval token.

candidates.name: Existing true model-provider path with Bossfang-owned loop

evidence.claim: Bossfang already owns a model/tool loop in its normal execution path.
Current UAR completion route executes a harness and is not this inference-only alternative.

risks: Cannot provide UAR execution semantics.
No actual model-only UAR endpoint has been established by this review.
candidates.decision_rationale: A coherent separate product mode using an actual inference provider; do not relabel current UAR endpoint as inference-only.

candidates.name: Codex app-server and Claude Agent SDK lifecycle contracts
candidates.fit_for_gap: F1/F5: comparison for explicit harness identity, approvals, cancellation and observation

evidence.claim: Official thread/turn/item and approval/interrupt contract informs harness distinction.
SDK owns agent execution loop; local adapter source remains authoritative for actual integration.

risks: Documentation comparison is not a reason to rewrite unrelated adapters.
Current remote docs may differ from installed CLI/SDK versions.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reference only execution identity (thread/turn versus task/run), exact approval identity, and interrupt acknowledgement/terminal classification; no new dependency or adapter rewrite.

candidates.name: Current nested completion-shaped UAR execution

evidence.claim: Calls UAR full-execution completion route and parses completion-shaped events.
Route creates RunExecutionRequest; supplied tools/history do not define one outer completion contract.

risks: Two reachable loop implementations and unshared attempt/cancel semantics.
Normal EndTurn is counterevidence to unconditional duplicate writes; failure consequences need reproduction.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reject for new UAR-delegated jobs; capability-based migration must not silently fall back to this path.

candidates.name: Existing UAR identity policy boundary
candidates.fit_for_gap: F2/F3/G7-A common inbound policy independent of downstream receiver inventory

evidence.claim: Existing verifier implements signature/claim checking; remote required-policy and cache freshness belong here.
Application-issued key authority requires role attenuation, tenant preservation and owner/admin revoke policy.
Host identity grant boundary must preserve typed host provenance separate from user-supplied roles.

risks: This does not choose an external IdP or implement receiver-side authorization.
Production module ownership must be agreed before writes.
candidates.decision_rationale: Concrete common policy adaptation can be specified without inventing a remote receiver; reuses cand-002 cryptography, no new service.

candidates.name: Existing provider/integration secret stores and conditional resource storage adapter
candidates.fit_for_gap: G7-B/F4 credential storage authority and its explicit remote gap

evidence.claim: AES-256-GCM provider-key encryption; not generic MCP refresh-token persistence.
Provider-specific scoped key lookup; do not reinterpret its schema as a remote token vault.
Desktop integration secret store uses safeStorage encryption and refuses unavailable/basic_text encryption on write.

risks: OS/backend availability and key custody need platform acceptance.
No remote tenant-aware MCP refresh-token store has been demonstrated.
candidates.decision_rationale: Reference current storage building blocks without overstating them; block remote resource-token persistence on REMOTE-RESOURCE-SECRET-STORE selection and acceptance. Storage categories: local OS-backed encrypted storage is reference-only for desktop; existing-backend owner/tenant-scoped encrypted persistence is conditional on custody/schema policy; existing external vault/KMS adapters are deferred until infrastructure is named. No new vault service or vendor library selected.

build_required.why_no_candidate: Existing crypto library handles signatures; only the application can define authority and deployment-specific claim/cache policy.

Static or JWT-auth-only checks cannot close it.
Existing exact host admission remains; product clients and pending-root decision plumbing require application-specific integration.

build_required.why_no_candidate: Library secret wrappers cannot define policy for product logs, persistence or tool-generated text.
